notes: Turn ids T1 to T59 number the speaker paragraphs of google-meet-transcript.txt in file order (the title, attendee, time and closing lines aren't turns). No speaker has two paragraphs in a row, so each paragraph is one turn.
alsoAccept lists other kinds a careful consultant could reasonably choose; a match on any of them counts.
Priya Govender is the consultant. Lindiwe Zulu, Graham Fortuin and Ayanda Ngcobo are the client, and all three agreed to the transcript and the local AI at T2 to T4.

Tricky cases: T21's '1,400 parent contacts' is corrected at T51 (U8 holds the corrected figure); T33's phones-not-computers is an assumption to be checked (U14); the nightly CSV export at T30 is the consultant's suggestion, deferred by the client at T31 (U13); the security rule is spread over T38 and T39 (U17); paying through the portal is explicitly ruled out at T18 (U6); the 'light portal' at T35 is the consultant's wording, agreed by Ayanda at T36 (U15).

findings.statement: Monthly fee statements and term reports are printed and sent home with the learners. Half the statements never reach parents, who then phone about fees they didn't know they owed, and the reports take the admin staff a week each term for about 900 learners.
Notices go out by email and on WhatsApp broadcast lists. The lists fill up (there are five now), and parents who change numbers drop off.
Absence notes are handwritten in the homework diary or emailed to the class teacher, and don't reliably reach the office: a learner was marked absent for three days with no reason known.
One place where a parent sees what they owe, their child's reports and the school's notices, and reports their child sick; and the school stops printing (a real cost, and many hours).
Parents see the current fee balance, the monthly statement as a PDF, and the reference to use for EFT.
No payments through the portal: the school doesn't take card payments and won't; parents keep paying by EFT or debit order.
findings.note: Sounds like a requirement (paying fees online) but is explicitly ruled out. Recording 'parents can pay fees in the portal' is wrong.

findings.statement: The term report, the same PDF that is printed, is released to every family on the same day.

On report day every parent logs in within a couple of hours, mostly in the evening, from about 1,650 parent contacts (corrected from 1,400). Last year a one-grade test of reports on the website took the site down.
findings.note: Ayanda says 1,400 at T21; Lindiwe corrects it to about 1,650 at T51 after checking SchoolBase. A finding that says 1,400 is wrong.

findings.statement: The office and grade heads send notices to the whole school, one grade or one team.
Parents submit an absence note (reason and dates) in the portal, and the class teacher and the office both see it straight away.
SchoolBase 7 (from about 2014) runs on a server in the admin block. It holds learners, parents, fees and marks, exports CSV, produces the report PDFs, and sends the emails.
How does the portal get fresh data from SchoolBase? Whether it has an API is unknown; the supplier hasn't answered.
The consultant proposed feeding the portal from a nightly CSV export from SchoolBase, so SchoolBase itself is never touched.
findings.note: The consultant's suggestion. Lindiwe worries balances would be out of date (parents pay on the 1st and phone on the 2nd) and defers it until the supplier replies: not agreed.

findings.statement: Most parents would use the portal on their phones rather than a computer. Graham believes so, but the school has never asked; to be checked.
findings.note: Stated as an unverified belief. Recording it as confirmed is a status error.

findings.statement: The portal must be light on mobile data (small pages, PDFs downloaded only when opened), because data is expensive for parents (Graham reckons most are on prepaid) and bursary families count every megabyte.
findings.note: Worded by the consultant at T35 and agreed by Ayanda at T36.

findings.statement: Could the portal be zero-rated with the mobile networks? The consultant will look into it.

Only a learner's own parents or guardians may see anything about that learner (reports, medical reasons on absence notes, addresses), and the office must be able to bar individual parents: about a dozen files have court orders.
findings.note: Spread over Graham's T38 and Lindiwe's T39; the consultant restates at T40 and Graham confirms at T41.

findings.statement: The board requires the portal to be hosted in South Africa.
Notices and the main screens also in isiZulu (for grandparents who care for learners), large clear text, and support for screen readers (a blind parent on the PTA).
Use the school's maroon, not a generic blue.
The finance committee proposes R250,000 for the first year, all in; the board must approve it at its meeting on 28 January, so a firm figure is needed for then.
findings.note: The figure is stated by the client; the approval is still pending, which the statement carries.

findings.statement: Parents should get the term-two reports (out on 26 June) through the portal.
Trial the portal with grade 8's term-one reports in April before the full roll-out, so a bad first report day doesn't cost parents' trust.
findings.note: Proposed by the consultant at T52 and agreed by Graham (T53) and Lindiwe (T54).

findings.statement: The school has one IT person, two days a week; if something breaks on report night, there is nobody.
Later, booking slots for parents' evenings; not now.

notFindings.why: The consent check at the start of the meeting is recorded on the consent form, not in the record.
Small talk about Ayanda's frozen camera; the school Wi-Fi isn't part of the portal.
The consultant's own follow-up (sending a summary) is an action, not a finding about the client.
